newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Helix drop said realistic correction.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Helix drop said realistic correction.

text.p: The sharp fall in the share price of junior Gawler Craton gold explorer Helix Resources NL was seen by analysts on Wednesday as a realistic correction, although they said the stock still held promise.
"To me it is a reality check," Paul Barnes, resource analyst with Macquarie Equities Ltd told Reuters.
"They got way out of whack with what they have proved up and the market got a little bit carried away with their upside exploration potential," he said.

Helix, which surged from 45 cents to A$4.99 in four months, had dropped to A$3.63 at 0140 GMT (12.40 p.m.) on Wednesday, after sagging to A$3.30 earlier in the day, following market disappointment with interim drilling results released Tuesday.

"The results were discouraging but they still have 40 metres of mineralisation and the calcrete anomaly goes for four kilometres .... (so) the story is not over by any stretch, they still have a lot more drilling to do," Barnes said.
The latest drilling results showed average grades of about 0.7 grams per tonne (g/t) of gold, against the grades of about 2.0 g/t reported late in 1996 that sparked Helix's share surge.
The best hole intersected 2.6 g/t over 44 metres from depths of 144 to 188 metres, including four metres at 21.1 g/t.
While the prospectivity of the ground of other stocks in the promising South Australian area had not changed, Helix was the current market driver, Barnes said.
"So until the other juniors come out with some results of their own, they will be going up and down on the back of Helix," he said.
Barnes said Helix's price should continue to fall, depending on the next results they published.
"I imagine they will be rushing things ahead to try to stem the flow," he said.
Howard Tweedie, analyst with Banque Nationale de Paris, said the jury was still out on Helix and that while the stock had got overheated, Tuesday's results were only interim.
"I would say (Helix's price) is coming back to more realistic levels," he said.
He said he did not think the situation was yet a disaster for Acacia Resources Ltd, which last week unveiled a 17.4 percent stake in Helix bought for A$38 million.
Tweedie said he believed the gold major had taken a long-term view of the stock and region.
Another analyst, who did not want to be named, said the market had been fairly quick to judge Helix on Tuesday's results.
"The trouble is the expectation was factored into the price already and anything less than exceptional results were going to (make it) pretty hard to maintain that share price," he said.
"Whether it has been an overcorrection or not, time will tell," he said.
